title: Support crate: Web Push delivery (RFC 8291, VAPID, retry)
description: Per JMAP-vjm0 (amended 2026-10-19) and AGENTS.md §Support crates. Deliver JMAP push payloads (RFC 8620 §7.2 PushSubscription, chatPush payloads from jmap-chat-server build_chat_message_push) via Web Push: RFC 8291 message encryption (aes128gcm, RFC 8188), RFC 8292 VAPID, TTL/Urgency/Topic headers (RFC 8030), retry with backoff, 404/410 -> subscription gone signal for the caller to destroy it. Also the RFC 8620 §7.2.2 PushVerification POST. First: check crates.io for maintained Web Push crates (e.g. web-push, and RFC 8291 encryption crates) and prefer a thin adapter. SSRF policy on the push URL and rate limits stay with the consumer (inputs/hooks). Not a dependency of any *-types or *-server crate. Consumers: chinwag now (chinwag-nuqe.8.*), kith/stoa/mimid later.
acceptance_criteria: Encryption tested against RFC 8291 Section 5 example (fixed keys, salt, plaintext -> exact ciphertext); VAPID JWT shape per RFC 8292 with a fixed key; retry/backoff and gone-subscription handling tested against a local HTTP stub; no *-server/*-types crate depends on it (cargo tree check).
close_reason: Committed and adversarially verified (batch 7); CI at 84a9b7bc
